security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline prop names, documentation links, and placeholder environment variable examples. Two command examples and one remote registry URL are confirmed as medium or low risk because they direct users to execute external package or skill installation commands. A semantic review also found a medium-risk workflow concern around agent-driven form filling with client-side tools.

remediation.issue: Remote install commands are shown in setup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin tool versions where possible, tell users to review the remote registry output before applying it, and document the exact files the command installs.

remediation.issue: Client-side tools can let an agent scan forms and fill fields.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before tool execution, scope tools to specific form refs, and block sensitive fields unless the host app allows them.

remediation.issue: API key setup is shown with an environment file placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: State that API keys must stay server-side, must not be committed, and should only be used through the proxy route.

semantic_findings.title: Agent-Driven Form Modification Requires Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The skill demonstrates client-side tools that let an agent scan a user interface and fill form fields. This is a legitimate feature, but it can alter user data or sensitive forms unless the host app scopes tools and requires approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented TSX example configures scoped client tools and a prompt that allows form filling. The security impact depends on host app controls, so confidence is high for the capability and moderate for exploitability.

content.user_title: Build Agent UIs for React and Next.js
content.value_statement: React teams need agent interfaces that handle streaming, tools, approvals, and rich responses without custom infrastructure. This skill shows how to add a ready agent component, proxy route, and scoped tool patterns.
actual_capabilities: Installs a shadcn-based Agent component into React and Next.js projects.
Shows a Next.js proxy route using the Inference SDK.
Documents streaming responses, tool lifecycle states, approvals, and widgets.
Demonstrates scoped browser tools for scanning forms and filling fields.
Lists component props for proxy URLs, agent configuration, file uploads, and image uploads.
limitations: The skill file does not include the full component source.
Setup depends on external packages and a remote shadcn registry URL.
A server-side Inference API key and proxy route are required.
Client-side tools need application-specific permission checks.

best_practices: Review remote registry output and package changes before merging installation commands.
Keep API keys in server-side environment variables and route all provider calls through the proxy.
Scope client-side tools narrowly and require user approval before changing form data.
anti_patterns: Running remote npx commands in a production branch without reviewing generated files.
Passing API keys or provider credentials into browser components.
Giving agent tools broad access to forms, files, uploads, or page state without controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you add an agent interface to React and Next.js applications using a shadcn-style component.

faq.question: Does it include backend logic?
faq.answer: It shows a Next.js proxy route that delegates to the Inference SDK. Your app still owns deployment and access control.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented setup uses an Inference API key that should stay in server-side environment variables.

faq.question: Can the agent use tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide shows scoped client-side tools and describes tool progress, approval states, and results.

faq.question: Is file upload supported?
faq.answer: The component props include options for file and image uploads. Enable them only when your app needs them.

faq.question: What should I review before installing?
faq.answer: Review the remote registry output, package additions, proxy route, API key handling, and any client-side tool permissions.
